text: This includes the suitability of the witness to give evidence via live video or live television link and the nature of the evidence that the witness will be giving.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Apart from arranging for such witnesses to give evidence by video in a separate room in the FJC, the Court may also permit a vulnerable witness to be accompanied by a trained Court volunteer recruited by the Singapore Children's Society, under the Vulnerable Witness Support Programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The trained volunteer will not only accompany the vulnerable witness during the Court proceedings, but will provide the witness with information about Court processes and procedures, and continue to provide the witness with emotional support after the hearing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Pillai spoke about ensuring that the housing needs of divorcing parties and children are addressed when the Court decides on the division of the matrimonial flat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The parties are required to provide key information on their HDB property as part of the divorce application.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In deciding the division of the matrimonial assets, the Court does consider the welfare and needs of the children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Court may also direct parties to seek HDB's views and consider information provided by HDB on, for example, the retention of the matrimonial flat and post-divorce housing options for the divorcing parties and their children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: There are also various support schemes put in place by HDB and MSF to ensure a smooth housing transition for divorcees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To equip parties with the knowledge and skills to make informed decisions regarding the matrimonial property that prioritises the child’s well-being, MSF's Family Assist Portal will provide parties with information on post-divorce housing options.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Court can refer divorcing parties to HDB for housing counselling before the divorce is finalised, for them to better understand their post-divorce housing options.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In deciding the division of the matrimonial flat, even when the parties have reached an agreement, the Court does consider the welfare and needs of the children and direct parties to seek HDB's views.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Court may consider information provided by HDB on, for example, the retention of the matrimonial flat and post-divorce housing options for the divorcing parties and their children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Nevertheless, we thank Mr Pillai for his suggestions and we will continue to study how the process relating to the division of the matrimonial flat may be strengthened to protect the interests of children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Ms Hany Soh has asked about the docketing system for divorce proceedings on the ordinary track.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: She also made suggestions on how a global settlement could be facilitated.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Whether a contested case is suitable for docketing to designated judges depends on the facts of the case.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Generally, high conflict cases and cases involving highly contentious issues on the custody, care and control of children, are docketed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As far as possible, docketing is done in the earlier stages of proceedings to allow a single judge to take charge of the case.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Presently, almost all contested cases are referred to mediation in the early stages of proceedings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Nonetheless, we thank Ms Soh for her suggestions and will certainly continue to study how we can improve therapeutic justice outcomes in all aspects of the divorce process.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan has asked about allowing the FJR to prescribe that judges may conduct interviews with children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Louis Chua has also made suggestions on training family judges to handle children in interviews with them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I mentioned in my opening speech the rationale behind this amendment, including the need for more clarity in the legislation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I also briefly mentioned that judicial interviews are not the only – nor the preferred – method of ascertaining a child's wishes, but will complement the variety of methods that can be used to hear the child's voice.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I would add that family judges do receive specialised training on whether, when and how to interview a child.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This training sensitises family judges to the needs of a child, the safety concerns and the potential impact the Court proceedings may have on the child.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Judicial interviews of children may also be conducted in the joint presence of FJC's Court Family Specialists who are proficient in interviewing children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Court Family Specialist is a trained professional and experienced counsellor, psychologist or social worker from the Counselling and Psychological Services (CAPS), which is the social science arm of the Family Justice Courts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked about the minimum age of children being interviewed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As the ability to communicate can differ across children of the same age, a different approach may be required for each child.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Courts have, however, held that judicial interviews would only be useful where the "children are mature enough to convey their views independently".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Women's Charter also provides that the child should be "of an age to express an independent opinion".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: They also often involve children, who will be worst affected by strained relationships and fractured family ties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is why “Therapeutic Justice” has been given much attention in implementing family proceedings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We want the Court process to nudge the family towards an outcome that is beneficial to all parties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We want to equip families involved with the necessary tools and resources so that they can move on and emerge from adversity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We do not wish to see families getting entangled in acrimonious litigation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Therefore, this Bill aims to enhance the therapeutic justice elements in the family justice system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These new reforms will complement some enhancements to the family justice system that have been implemented by MSF and MinLaw, together with the Family Justice Court (FJC), over the years to make family proceedings less acrimonious.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Today, in Parliament, the Family Justice Reform Bill will introduce major changes to the maintenance enforcement process.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Over the years, we have progressively refined the maintenance enforcement framework.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: However, we still see a relatively high number of cases against those who refuse to comply with the maintenance order.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have received feedback on the anxiety, frustration and other real-life impact on the applicant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These changes are intended to address the needs from the feedback.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Parties no longer need to apply to Court and go through a formal legal process to gather evidence on the assets and means of the parties involved.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MEO will submit this information to the Court, and the Court can use this information when making a judgment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As a result, this will save time as there is no need to attend multiple Court hearings, save money because there is no need to pay legal fees, and reduce hardship as there is no need to prove the asset and the ability of the parties involved for the parties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is hoped that this latest reform will help to further strengthen the family justice system by reducing acrimony, pain and suffering of families and the children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, I will now conclude.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The amendments in this Bill will simplify and make family proceedings more efficient.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: They will also reduce acrimony in family proceedings, strengthening Therapeutic Justice in the family justice system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will also continue to work closely with our partners in the legal community and social services, such as the DSSAs, to provide more avenues of support to individuals who may nevertheless find the process challenging.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Where the financial needs of the families who have undergone a breakdown are met in a timely manner, this will go a long way towards helping families to heal and move on from the breakdown of the family unit, in a positive manner.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Divorced parents will also be able to better focus on co-parenting in a manner which best protects their children’s interests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Melvin Yong brought up the importance of strengthening marriages and families, thereby reducing the number of families who have to go through the painful process of divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Indeed, this is MSF’s belief, and efforts have been put across all life stages through various Government initiatives to support families through their life journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Such efforts span supporting families in setting strong foundations in marriage and parenting, in the cost of raising their children, in navigating and overcoming difficulties and in ageing well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These are efforts that we continually build on, and proposals from Members on how we can make further strides in this regard are always welcome.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Members have expressed their concern regarding a family’s ability to move on financially post-divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about support provided to families early to sort out their finances when a marriage has broken down.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This includes information on the impact of divorce on finances and housing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: A personalised tool will also be launched on the portal soon to help citizens better understand their post-divorce HDB housing options.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked if financial counselling can be incorporated into the Co-Parenting Programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Like I mentioned earlier in my opening speech, we have made it mandatory for all divorcing parents with minor children to go through the Co-Parenting Programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Today, the Co-Parenting Programme covers practical issues arising from a divorce, including modules on making housing arrangements and managing finances.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: During the Co-Parenting Programme consultation sessions, counsellors may also refer parties to financial counselling services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Louis Chua asked about financial assistance for those referred to the SSOs under the maintenance enforcement process.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The details will need to be worked out with the set-up of the new unit of Maintenance Enforcement Officers (MEOs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This includes interim assistance for cases requiring urgent assistance, such as if maintenance is not being paid and has resulted in financial difficulties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It was heartening to hear from Ms Yeo Wan Ling about the work that NTUC’s Women and Family Unit is doing to support single mothers and divorcees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MSF believes in the importance of caring for and supporting women in such vulnerable situations and had announced several efforts as part of the 2022 White Paper on Singapore Women’s Development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This includes partnerships between the Government and community partners under the Alliance for Action to Strengthen Marriages and Family Relationships.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As an example, MSF's community partner HCSA has updated their portal SPIN which stands for Single Parents Informed, Involved, Included to address questions divorcees may have towards housing and childcare arrangements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MSF is focused on ensuring that childcare arrangements do not exact a burden on single or divorced parents so that they are able to seek employment and provide for themselves and their family members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We welcome partnerships with NTUC's Women and Family Unit to further enable single or divorced parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Louis Chua had raised the issue of divorced parents being unable to come to an agreement on their child's educational arrangements and their housing arrangements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We think it best for parents to work out suitable arrangements cooperatively and encourage them to do so outside of the Court system, bearing in mind what would be in their children's best interest.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is for this reason that we have made it mandatory for all divorcing couples with minor children to go through the Co-Parenting Programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is not ideal for parents to seek to rely on Court orders to exhaustively list the decision rights for all matters pertaining to their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On the issue of school arrangements, in particular, something as important as a school transfer, parents who have joint custody of their child need to come to a common agreement on the child's school transfer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I hope Members can understand that schools have to be seen to be fair to both parents and it is not ideal for divorced spouses to bring their differences to the school to be the arbiter.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our housing policies prioritise our limited housing supply for households with the greatest need, such as those that involve children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As such, divorcees with children are a family nucleus and can apply for public housing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For divorcees without children, they can retain their matrimonial flat alone if they are at least 35 years old.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: If they are below 35 years old, they can retain their flat if they include a family member, such as either of their parents, to form an eligible family nucleus.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: HDB does allow divorcees below age 35 without children to retain their matrimonial flat on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Leon Perera had asked whether we would consider providing for maintenance for ex-husbands and men.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This has been raised on several occasions by various Members of Parliament, including Ms Carrie Tan and Mr Ang Wei Neng.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I would also add that the Courts have also refrained from granting higher amounts of maintenance to wives who are able to work, even if they had not worked or stopped working for some years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Courts' goal is to award reasonable maintenance such that it will meet the financial needs of the wife until such time that she could secure for herself some form of employment and adjust to her post-divorce situation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The MEP is a big step towards ensuring that families are able to resolve issues surrounding maintenance that may arise post-divorce, in an effective and non-acrimonious way.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is a key piece that we are adding to our comprehensive landscape of marriage and divorce support, to give every family the best possible chance of achieving good outcomes despite the ups and downs in life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are confident that when the MEP takes effect, it will make a meaningful difference in terms of ensuring sustainable maintenance payment outcomes for all parties involved.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I would just end by reiterating my thanks to the various stakeholders in the family justice ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And with that, Sir, I beg to move.
